rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Referent resolution under a sequential deck read.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Harm check: rule exists so a reader is never asked to resolve a term against nothing. Walked all 10 chunks in order. Chunk2 line8 'The scoped task you picked as homework' is self-explaining via the bolded sizing rule two lines below (line10) and by the section's own topic; not a dangling referent. Chunk2 lines14/16 'that essay warns against' resolves to the essay named in the same sentence. Chunk4 line31 'The map has a far side' is the compendium's own listed arc-earned exempt term (rule 1's carve-out lists 'the map' verbatim as an example). Chunk4 line27 'a bug fix, a plan read' are backward refs, scored under rule 3, not rule 1. Chunk5 line51 'The run started from a pinned commit' — 'run' is used generically for the agent session, resolvable without a prior named antecedent (plain-English noun use, not a term requiring earning). Chunk6's four bullets each name their own referent inline (Gauntlet Loop, Wayfinder skill, '10% smaller' codebase target, disposable branch). Chunk9 'this session' / `task.md` resolves against the student's own live M4 session per the session-artifact carve-out. No unresolved referent found.

Ran: grep -n 'Module [0-9]\|that essay\|the essay\|the opening' curriculum/trainings/agentic-engineering-101/run-the-first-experiment.md, restricted to lines <84 (body) -> hits at 14, 16, 62, 66, 68. Line14 names its source in-sentence ('Simon Willison's [Designing agentic loops]...if still on your list from Module 3/Module 2' behind a per-cohort content flag) — named by title, not positioned. Line16 names '[Why Software Factories Fail]...in the gap after Module 1' directly by title. Lines 62/66/68 name 'Module 5' as a forward pointer to a real module, not a positional 'the next module said'. Chunk6's four external items are each named by author + title ('Matt Shumer's Gauntlet Loop', 'Matt Pocock's Wayfinder skill'), never by page position. No bare positional callback found anywhere in the body.

Verified all 7 in-body include-link targets under 'Start here' exist on disk: ls curriculum/lectures/ | grep -E 'the-far-half|the-agent-loop|test-and-learn|ironies-of-automation|what-keeps-a-long-running' -> all 5 found; ls curriculum/exercises/ | grep -E 'walk-and-send-off|set-the-markers' -> both found. rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Live-demo beats survive a text read.
rules_evaluated.evidence: No guess-before-reveal live-demo instruction appears anywhere in this module file's body. This is a thin module file (metadata + Bloom LOs + ordered include-links); any such beat lives in the linked lectures/exercises, judged on their own slides pass when those files are fired.

Checked all 10 chunks for a self-carrying claim vs. a bare wait-state fragment. Thinnest content chunk is 'Big Idea' at 2 sentences / ~14 words, but it states the module's own thesis standalone ('Prep your first long session. The session is how you find out what's missing.'). No chunk matches the orphan example shape (a single context-dependent bullet or wait-state).

Checked all 10 headers against their own chunk content. Closest call: 'Key Concepts' (chunk5) is phrased in past tense ('The audit ranked...', 'You corrected...') describing exercises the student has not yet done at this point in the deck's linear order (they follow in 'Start here', chunk4, which precedes it) — but 'Key Concepts' is a canonical module-shape.md recap section read as a standing summary of the module's substance, not a sequential narration, matching house convention across all six AE101 modules; the header stays literally true of its content either way. No header is contradicted by its own chunk.

Ran: grep -niE 'not .*\. not .*\.' run-the-first-experiment.md -> no match. grep -niE 'one of the most|most useful|most powerful|incredibly|extremely useful|best way' -> no match. Manual read for anaphora/epistrophe triples -> none found; the 'no plan.md, no verifier, no reference artifact' lists (chunk3 line23, chunk5 line49) are plain three-item enumerations of what is absent, not rhetorical repetition of a repeated clause-opening. No number-plus-retraction hedge (chunk5's 'worst two or three' and chunk6's '10% smaller' are plain claims, not hedge-then-retract). No abstraction-noun stacks (all nouns are concrete: plan.md, verifier, reference artifact, pinned commit, throwaway branch). No verb triplets with an empty leg. All six sub-patterns absent across all 10 chunks.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Emphasis budget — bold is for handles, and go very lightly.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Harm check: rule exists so bold reliably signals a named handle, not decoration; a bold that isn't a handle costs the reader's trust in every other bold on the slide. Located every bold span in the body fresh: grep -n '\*\*' lines<84 -> line10 (mandated check_pedagogy.md §34 task-sizing floor+ceiling callout, sits in ## Prework — N/A by name); lines20/21/22/23 (## What You'll Learn LO-verb template, one word each — N/A by name); lines72/74/76/78 (Pre-reads menu, mode-word-only 'Read,'/'Watch,'/'Read,'/'Read (longer),', title left plain — N/A by the reading-list waiver). Line29, chunk4 'Start here': '**The question, to you:** which task have you been putting off because it needs hours of babysitting?' — a bolded rhetorical address opening the room-discussion prompt. It is not a named law/governor/coined-term/checklist-item, and 'Start here' is none of the three sections rule 9 names as exempt (§34 callouts live in Prework/Bring-to-Module/Next; LO template lives in What-You'll-Learn only). Functionally this reads as a kicker before the actual question — the exact shape rule 9 bans categorically ('Kickers/koans/quotes never bold'), independent of the per-slide budget (this chunk carries only this one bold, well inside ≤1). Checked for an existing accept-note: grep -n 'Slide size accepted\|Slide deixis accepted\|kicker' run-the-first-experiment.md -> none. The fix (unbold the lead-in) would not degrade the beat — the room-discussion question still lands as plain narrative — so this is filed as a genuine TODO, not suppressed as a rule question.
